email.description: Never null: a cleaned-up user's grants are all revoked before the address is cleared (lifecycle.rs cleanup_user), and the member list only returns unrevoked grants.

AccessWorkspaceContext.description: Personal owner-private projection omits object_visibility entirely. A platform reader may see only shared metadata, with no membership role.

token.description: One-time invitation value; returned only at creation. Never an example, URL, log entry or list field.

AccessApproverRequest.description: Approver queue projection. Ineligible requester email and display name are both redacted to null; submitted workspace name stays a frozen snapshot.

AccessMapping.description: Two closed variants mirroring the oidc_group_mappings CHECK constraint (0001_enterprise.sql): target_kind platform requires platform_role and no workspace fields; target_kind workspace requires workspace_id and workspace_role and no platform_role.

digest.description: A preview of a NOT-YET-SAVED mapping has no stored state to confirm, so the digest is always null.

immediate.description: A not-yet-saved mapping has no grants to revoke; the evaluator's fixed default (group_mapping_preview.rs).

diff.description: email is never null: preview rows exclude cleaned-up users (lifecycle.rs preview_platform_effect/preview_workspace_effect: usr.cleaned_at IS NULL) and an immediate row names only unrevoked grants, which cleanup revokes before clearing the address. A new mapping can only add access: grants are compared with the existing ones, never removed (existing_mapping_id is null), so the *_lost lists are always empty.

digest.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the stored mapping (directory.rs mapping_digest), the value a later If-Match must quote.

oneOf.description: No stored grant changes (an unchanged merge): the default of evaluate().

immediate.description: The management write's own immediate effect, present with applies:true only when the write would revoke grants (a delete, or a merge that changes a field).

diff.description: email is never null: preview rows exclude cleaned-up users (lifecycle.rs preview_platform_effect/preview_workspace_effect: usr.cleaned_at IS NULL) and an immediate row names only unrevoked grants, which cleanup revokes before clearing the address. A row is `gained` when the after rank is above the before rank (so after is never null) and `lost` when it is below (so before is never null)

AccessWorkspaceAccess.description: Workspace-scoped effective access (GET /workspaces/{ws}/access): no key is bound, so key_id is null, the key layer is the inactive stub (applies=false, null limits/budgets/catalogs/restriction), and the key layer and the key_restriction reason are never emitted. EXACTLY ONE of budgets (the stacked form) or monthly_budget_microusd with an optional budget_period (the deprecated single-budget form) must be present: both, or neither, or budget_period with budgets, are refused. issuer.description: An https URL without credentials, query or fragment, at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes (directory.rs mapping_valid counts bytes; the schema's maxLength counts characters, so a multibyte value of at most 2048 characters can exceed the handler's limit). The handler accepts what the WHATWG URL parser (reqwest::Url::parse) accepts with scheme https, a host, no user info, no query and no fragment. The schema pattern is a deliberately narrower subset: the literal form https://host[:port][/path], a host without whitespace, control characters or / ? # @ : [ ] % < > ^ | \, and a port of 0 to 65535 (an empty port is accepted, as by the parser). Remaining differences, each probed over HTTP: (1) the parser trims leading and trailing whitespace, strips tab, CR and LF anywhere and also accepts https:host, https:/host, https:///host and a backslash as the path separator (https://host\path), none of which the schema accepts; (2) the parser percent-decodes the host (a host containing %75 is read as u), which the schema refuses with its % exclusion, and refuses what IDNA or IPv4 parsing refuses (a numeric host outside the IPv4 range, a bracketed host that is not an IPv6 address), which the schema accepts because it checks characters only; (3) leading zeros beyond five port digits (https://host:000080) are accepted by the parser and refused by the schema; (4) spaces, other control characters (C0 and C1) and a no-break space in the path are accepted by the parser (they are percent-encoded) and refused by the schema; empty user info (https://@host) is accepted by the parser and the handler (the username is empty and there is no password) and refused by the schema's @ exclusion; (5) a development installation (GATEWAY_ENV=development) additionally accepts http on a loopback host, which the schema never does (the setting is process-wide, so it is probed only as a refusal outside development).

patch_api_v1_platform_oidc_group_mapping.description: Fields merged onto the stored mapping (an omitted field keeps its value, an explicit null clears platform_role, workspace_id or workspace_role) and then validated as a complete mapping. Cross-field rule, as far as the body decides it: when target_kind is present, platform requires a platform_role and null workspace_id and workspace_role, and workspace requires a workspace_id and workspace_role (admin or member) and a null platform_role, each for the fields the body names (directory.rs mapping_valid on the merged row). Without target_kind the stored row's kind decides, which the schema cannot see: a body that names only a workspace field for a platform mapping is accepted by the schema and refused by the handler. When target_kind is present, fields the body omits are still filled from the stored row: switching a platform mapping to workspace without also sending platform_role:null keeps the stored platform_role, so the schema accepts that body and the handler refuses it.

The handler accepts what the WHATWG URL parser (reqwest::Url::parse) accepts with scheme https, a host, no user info, no query and no fragment. The schema pattern is a deliberately narrower subset: the literal form https://host[:port][/path], a host without whitespace, control characters or / ? # @ : [ ] % < > ^ | \, and a port of 0 to 65535 (an empty port is accepted, as by the parser). Remaining differences, each probed over HTTP: (1) the parser trims leading and trailing whitespace, strips tab, CR and LF anywhere and also accepts https:host, https:/host, https:///host and a backslash as the path separator (https://host\path), none of which the schema accepts; (2) the parser percent-decodes the host (a host containing %75 is read as u), which the schema refuses with its % exclusion, and refuses what IDNA or IPv4 parsing refuses (a numeric host outside the IPv4 range, a bracketed host that is not an IPv6 address), which the schema accepts because it checks characters only; (3) leading zeros beyond five port digits (https://host:000080) are accepted by the parser and refused by the schema; (4) spaces, other control characters (C0 and C1) and a no-break space in the path are accepted by the parser (they are percent-encoded) and refused by the schema; empty user info (https://@host) is accepted by the parser and the handler (the username is empty and there is no password) and refused by the schema's @ exclusion; (5) a development installation (GATEWAY_ENV=development) additionally accepts http on a loopback host, which the schema never does (the setting is process-wide, so it is probed only as a refusal outside development).

group_value.description: OIDC group value: 1 to 512 UTF-8 bytes of the value as sent (directory.rs mapping_valid counts bytes, without trimming), no control characters. The schema's maxLength counts characters, so a multibyte value of at most 512 characters can exceed the handler's limit.

post_api_v1_platform_oidc_group_mappings.description: The PATCH merge body plus an optional delete flag (a boolean). The handler previews a DELETE when delete is true OR when no mapping field is present (group_mapping_preview.rs: is_delete = delete || patch.is_empty()), so {} and {"delete":false} both preview a delete, while {"delete":false,"enabled":true} previews the merge. With delete:true every other mapping field is ignored and its value is not validated ({"delete":true,"enabled":"x"} succeeds), although an unknown key is still refused with 422; the schema keeps typing those fields (a wildcard value is not expressible), so it refuses such a body that the handler accepts. Cross-field rule, as far as the body decides it: when target_kind is present, platform requires a platform_role and null workspace_id and workspace_role, and workspace requires a workspace_id and workspace_role (admin or member) and a null platform_role, each for the fields the body names (directory.rs mapping_valid on the merged row). Without target_kind the stored row's kind decides, which the schema cannot see: a body that names only a workspace field for a platform mapping is accepted by the schema and refused by the handler. When target_kind is present, fields the body omits are still filled from the stored row: switching a platform mapping to workspace without also sending platform_role:null keeps the stored platform_role, so the schema accepts that body and the handler refuses it.

anyOf.description: Workspace name (mod.rs valid_name): not blank after trimming, no control characters and at most 120 UTF-8 bytes of the value as sent (the handler counts bytes, without trimming). The schema's maxLength counts characters, so a multibyte name of at most 120 characters can exceed the handler's limit.

Workspace name (mod.rs valid_name): not blank after trimming, no control characters and at most 120 UTF-8 bytes of the value as sent (the handler counts bytes, without trimming). The schema's maxLength counts characters, so a multibyte name of at most 120 characters can exceed the handler's limit.

patch_api_v1_workspaces_by_wsRequest.description: Closed serde object or positional struct array in declared field order. Handler semantic validation (documented per field) applies.

email.description: The handler trims and lower-cases the value, then (directory.rs email_valid) requires exactly one '@' with a non-empty local part and domain, no whitespace or control characters and at most 320 UTF-8 bytes of the TRIMMED, LOWER-CASED text (lower-casing can lengthen it: U+0130 grows from 2 to 3 bytes). The schema's maxLength counts characters of the value as sent, untrimmed: it refuses a padded value the handler accepts and accepts a multibyte or lower-case-expanding value the handler refuses.

prefixItems.description: The handler trims and lower-cases the value, then (directory.rs email_valid) requires exactly one '@' with a non-empty local part and domain, no whitespace or control characters and at most 320 UTF-8 bytes of the TRIMMED, LOWER-CASED text (lower-casing can lengthen it: U+0130 grows from 2 to 3 bytes). The schema's maxLength counts characters of the value as sent, untrimmed: it refuses a padded value the handler accepts and accepts a multibyte or lower-case-expanding value the handler refuses.

post_api_v1_workspaces_by_ws_invitations.description: Closed serde object or positional struct array in declared field order. Handler semantic validation (documented per field) applies.

post_api_v1_workspaces_by_ws_membersRequ.description: Closed serde object or positional struct array in declared field order. Handler semantic validation (documented per field) applies.

AccessPlatformMapping.description: A platform-role group mapping: platform_role set, every workspace field null.

AccessWorkspaceMapping.description: A Team or Project workspace-role group mapping: workspace_id, workspace_role (admin or member) and the live workspace name and kind set, platform_role null.

AccessApprovedRequest.description: Decision response of an approve call: requester-private projection (no requester identity) after the decision. decided_by and decided_at are always set, and the applied membership grant is always present.

AccessDeniedRequest.description: Decision response of a deny call: requester-private projection (no requester identity) after the decision. decided_by and decided_at are always set; a denial never carries a membership grant.

AccessBudgetWindow.description: One budget window as a platform reader sees it: usage is always visible. Three shapes: known (no unknown-cost request; remaining_microusd is a decimal), unknown (at least one unknown-cost request: every figure is present but remaining_microusd is null) and unavailable (the accounting row is unreadable: used_microusd, unresolved_usage, exhausted, settled_microusd, pending_held_microusd, unknown_held_microusd, unknown_cost_requests and remaining_microusd are all null together and headroom_status is unknown). A null group therefore implies headroom_status unknown, but unknown does not imply the null group (governance/totals.rs read_budget_report and BudgetReport::remaining, policies.rs budget_windows).
